# telegram-bot-ui

> Design, build and audit Telegram bot UIs and the Bot API features behind them: texts, inline/reply keyboards, colored and disabled buttons, premium icons from one consistent set, force_reply forms, navigation, streaming AI replies with Stop (sendRichMessageDraft, can_stop, stopped_message_generation), ephemeral personal replies in groups, Rich Messages (tables, quotes, documents, embedded buttons), HTML widgets (sendWidget, widget_query, shared widgets, TON wallet), topics, formatting (HTML, MarkdownV2, entities), localization, plus the server side they need (allowed_updates, callback state, cancellation, retries, SDK gaps) and 10.3/10.4 gift, community, theme, managed-bot and verification updates. Use for "improve this bot's menu", "add a Stop button", "private answer in a group", "send a widget", "the bot feels frozen", "can't parse entities", "use the latest Bot API". Do NOT use for webhook/DevOps setup, databases, payment processing or auth unrelated to these features, or Microsoft .rtf files.

An Agent Skill. Start with `SKILL.md`; open other files only when the task needs them. Paths are relative to the skill folder. Capabilities:

- Build and audit bot interfaces: texts, inline and reply keyboards, colored and disabled buttons, navigation, forms, streaming AI replies with Stop, ephemeral replies in groups, Rich Messages, tables, formatting, localization.
- Product flows and use cases: shops, support, AI assistants, trackers, communities: stale buttons, double submit, audience leaks.
- Publish to Telegram channels: compose, validate, preview, approve, schedule and publish channel posts without double posting.
- Operate as an agent through a bot: allowlisted operators, approval-bound actions, prompt injection in inbound messages, MCP bridge.
- Build HTML widgets: Bot API 10.4 widgets: size limit, production context, caption and text fallback, widget_query, shared widgets, TON wallet.
- Look up the whole Bot API: methods, types and fields from a local catalog; validate a payload before sending; never invent a field.

## Entry point

- [Telegram Bot UI](SKILL.md): Portable, SDK-agnostic skill for the full life cycle of a **Telegram bot's user interface**: audit → screen/state map → text, buttons...

## Tools

- [audit_copy.py](scripts/audit_copy.py): Audit a localized message catalog for interface consistency. Offline.
- [audit_icons.py](scripts/audit_icons.py): Audit a bot's icon system: one consistent custom-emoji family per bot.
- [build_adapters.py](scripts/build_adapters.py): Generate every host-specific entry file from SKILL.md and adapters/routing.json.
- [install.py](scripts/install.py): Install, update or remove the telegram-bot-ui skill for one or more agent hosts.
- [render_registry.py](scripts/render_registry.py): Render references/bot-api-10.3-10.4.md from recipes/registry.json.
- [run_checks.py](scripts/run_checks.py): Run every offline check of the skill. No token, no network.
- [run_evals.py](scripts/run_evals.py): Validate the eval set, or execute its activation cases against a host CLI.
- [validate_keyboard.py](scripts/validate_keyboard.py): Validate Telegram button payloads: inline, reply and rich-message buttons.
- [validate_references.py](scripts/validate_references.py): Validate the skill's internal references and links.
- [validate_rich.py](scripts/validate_rich.py): Check an InputRichMessage (or a sendRichMessage / draft payload) offline.
- [validate_skill.py](scripts/validate_skill.py): Validate this skill's SKILL.md against the Agent Skills format.
- [validate_widget.py](scripts/validate_widget.py): Check an HTML widget before sendWidget (Bot API 10.4). Offline, no token.
